name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a system-level theme preference: default to dark mode, but let users override it with a one-click toggle. This keeps the interface consistent with Manus and Graphify’s dark themes while respecting individual preference, which improves enjoyment and clarity. The trade-off is a slight increase in initial setup complexity, but the benefit of aligning with our competitive analysis and user flexibility outweighs it.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t setup complexity—it’s alienating users who *prefer* light mode because they associate dark themes with eye strain or readability issues. A one-click toggle still forces users to manually correct the default, which violates the "real-not-display" rule. The better alternative: respect the OS/browser preference first, then let users override it—this respects actual user comfort without extra work. Settle it by testing both approaches with users who default to light mode.

name: Facet

Ship EXCAVA with a system-level theme preference that defaults to dark mode but respects the user’s OS-level setting. This ensures consistency with Manus and Graphify while removing the manual toggle’s friction—users who prefer light mode won’t need to override it. The trade-off is losing the one-click override’s explicitness, but we gain adherence to system standards, which improves clarity and enjoyment by aligning with how users already work.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk is assuming OS/browser settings reflect user preference—many users never change defaults, and some prefer light mode despite system settings. A better alternative: ship with a *user-level* theme preference that defaults to dark but respects a one-click override, settling the argument with a quick usability test measuring preference changes after first launch.
